Guidance: Provide a summary-level description of the project or phase: what it was, its purpose, and its boundaries. Keep it to a summary, and point to the project charter for detail.

Describe how the final product, service, or result achieved the benefits the project was undertaken to address. Identify the benefit and the evidence that it was realised, distinguishing a benefit that was realised from one that is still only expected.
The current realisation status of each benefit, and who owns tracking it after the project team has been released. A benefit with no owner at closure is a benefit that will not be measured.
Describe how the final product, service, or result achieved the business needs identified in the business plan.
Any business need that was not met, and what happens next now that the project is closed. A need left unstated here will be assumed met by whoever inherits the product.
Describe the scope objectives needed to achieve the planned benefits of the project.
Document the specific and measurable criteria needed to complete the scope objectives. State each one so that it can be answered met or not met, and cross-reference the scope baseline.
Provide the evidence that the completion criteria were met. Give the source of the evidence, such as the document, test result, or acceptance record, and not only the conclusion drawn from it.
Describe the quality objectives and criteria needed to achieve the planned benefits of the project.
Document the specific and measurable criteria needed to meet the product and project quality objectives.
Enter the verification and validation information from the product acceptance form. Cross-reference that form rather than restating it, so the two records cannot drift apart.
The planned time objectives: the approved schedule baseline duration and the planned completion date.
The actual completion date and the actual duration.

The difference between planned and actual, in days or weeks, with the reason. Where the project finished early, say so and explain why, because an unexplained favourable variance hides a planning error just as a delay does.
Any consequence of the time variance for the organization, such as a missed market window, and anything still open at closure.
The approved cost baseline, or the total budget at completion if no baseline applies.
The actual total spent at completion, stating whether it includes contingency drawn or reserve released.
The difference between planned and actual, in currency and as a percentage, with the reason.
Any consequence of the cost variance for the organization, such as a claim or a budget transfer still required, and anything still open.
The risk or issue, and where it came from. Give the reference from the risk or issue register rather than restating it.
What was done about it and how effective that was. Say plainly whether it worked.
What remains open, and who owns it after closure. An unresolved item transferred without a named recipient has not been transferred.
The contracts closed out, with the final value and the closure date of each. Where procurement was not used, state that plainly rather than leaving the section blank.
The obligations, warranties, and service levels met, transferred, or still outstanding, with the holder named for each.
Any claim or dispute settled before closure, and any that was not. An unresolved claim is a liability the project is handing on.
